description: Row-wise top-k selection among each row's first lengths[r] candidates, writing positions (or page-table slots) padded with -1. sglang topk_transform / fast_topk_v2, aiter top-k kernels, the selection half of a DSA indexer when it is a separate launch.

n_candidates.doc: candidates per row (the context length for an indexer)

call: Return the selected positions. If the entry maps positions through a page table, return the positions before the mapping or add the page table as an input and compare mapped slots with exact/multiset_rows.

timing.cache: scores were just written by the score kernel and are L2-resident for short rows; read-evict is the long-context condition.

negative_controls: select topk-1 and duplicate the last: valid_count/duplicate rejections
drop the lengths mask: positions beyond the row length appear (out_of_range or different_scores)
pitfalls: Compare indices as a selection, not as numbers: a relative tol on int outputs accepts 1000 for 1001, an exact compare rejects a legal tie order. topk_equivalent compares the selected scores.

A permutation score row has no ties; real scores (e.g. ReLU-clipped indexer logits, many exact zeros) tie heavily. Add a case whose scores carry ties (override dist to a coarse int_range cast to float) so the tie path is exercised.
Do not gate quality with sum(cand)/sum(ref) of selected scores: on long rows it is ~1.0 for almost any selection; normalize to the achievable range or use topk_equivalent.
One block per row: a kernel 'flat in batch' is under-occupied, not saturated; a candidate that splits rows changes the dispatch ladder, so cover the small-row decode buckets in replay.
